title: Erdős Problem #700: GCD of n with Binomial Coefficients
description: Study f(n) = min_{1<k≤n/2} gcd(n, C(n,k)). When does f(n) = n/P(n)? Are there ∞ many n with f(n) > √n? Is f(n) ≪ n/(log n)^A? Known: f(pq) = p, f(p²) ≥ p. Open.

meta.assumptions: 5 axioms: f_upper_bound, f_lower_bound, f_semiprime, erdos_700_question2, erdos_700_question3. fBinom now defined (not axiomatized). f_prime_square proved from f_lower_bound.

sections.title: Problem Statement and Imports
sections.summary: Module docstring introducing Erdos Problem #700: study $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \le n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$ with three open questions on characterization, large values, and upper bounds. Imports `Mathlib.Tactic`, `Nat.Basic`, `Nat.GCD.Basic`, `Nat.Choose.Basic`, `Nat.Prime.Basic`.
sections.mathContext: Erdos-Szekeres study $f(n)$, the minimum GCD of $n$ with its non-trivial binomial coefficients. Three questions: (1) characterize $\{n : f(n) = n/P(n)\}$, (2) infinitely many $n$ with $f(n) > \sqrt{n}$?, (3) $f(n) \ll_A n/(\log n)^A$? Known: $f(pq) = p$ for primes $p \le q$, $f(p^2) \ge p$, $f(30) = 6$.

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines `largestPrimeFactor` $P(n)$ via `Finset.sup` over prime divisors (returns 0 for $n \le 1$), `smallestPrimeFactor` $p(n)$ via `Nat.minFac`, and `fBinom` $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \leq n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$ as `Finset.min'` over `Finset.Icc 2 (n/2)` (nonempty for $n \ge 4$, returns 0 otherwise).
sections.mathContext: $P(n) = \sup\{p \in [0, n] : p \text{ prime}, p \mid n\}$. $p(n) = \text{Nat.minFac}(n)$. $f(n) = \min\{\gcd(n, \binom{n}{k}) : 2 \le k \le n/2\}$ for $n \ge 4$. The function $f$ measures the minimum common divisor between $n$ and its non-trivial binomial coefficients, detecting the arithmetic structure of $n$ through Pascal's triangle.

sections.title: Helper Lemmas
sections.summary: Proves `minFac_prime_sq` ($\text{minFac}(p^2) = p$) via `dvd_of_dvd_pow` and prime uniqueness. Proves `minFac_mul_prime` ($\text{minFac}(pq) = p$ for primes $p \le q$) via case analysis on which prime factor the minFac divides. Proves `le_largestPrimeFactor`: any prime factor $r \mid n$ satisfies $r \le P(n)$.
sections.mathContext: Lemma `minFac_prime_sq`: $\text{minFac}(p^2)$ is prime and divides $p^2$, hence divides $p$ by `dvd_of_dvd_pow`, and equals $p$ since $p$ is prime. Lemma `minFac_mul_prime`: $\text{minFac}(pq)$ divides $pq$, so divides $p$ or $q$; combined with $\text{minFac}(pq) \le p$ (from `minFac_le_of_dvd`), yields $\text{minFac}(pq) = p$. These are used in proving $f(pq) = p$ and $f(p^2) \ge p$.

sections.title: Basic Sandwich Bounds
sections.summary: Axiomatizes `f_upper_bound` ($f(n) \le n/P(n)$ for composite $n$, via Kummer's theorem) and `f_lower_bound` ($p(n) \le f(n)$ for $n \ge 2$, since the smallest prime dividing $n$ divides every $\gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$).
sections.mathContext: The sandwich inequality $p(n) \le f(n) \le n/P(n)$ is the fundamental structural result. Upper bound: choosing $k = p^a$ where $p^a \| n$ gives exactly one carry in base-$p$ addition, so $v_p(\binom{n}{k}) = 1$, hence $\gcd(n, \binom{n}{p^a}) = n/p^a \le n/P(n)$. Lower bound: for every $0 < k < n$, Kummer's theorem gives $v_p(\binom{n}{k}) \ge 1$ when $p \mid n$.

sections.title: Known Exact Values
sections.summary: PROVES `f_semiprime`: $f(pq) = p$ for primes $p \le q$, by sandwiching between `f_lower_bound` (giving $p \le f(pq)$) and `f_upper_bound` (giving $f(pq) \le pq/P(pq) \le p$). Axiomatizes `f_30`: $f(30) = 6 = 30/5$, the first non-semiprime example achieving $f(n) = n/P(n)$.
sections.mathContext: Proved: $f(pq) = p$ for primes $p \le q$. Lower bound: $p = \text{minFac}(pq) \le f(pq)$. Upper bound: $f(pq) \le pq/P(pq)$, and $q \le P(pq)$ (since $q$ is a prime factor), so $pq/P(pq) \le pq/q \cdot P(pq)/P(pq) \le p$. The case $n = 30 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$ with $f(30) = 6$ shows the characterization extends beyond semiprimes.

sections.title: Question 1: Characterization of f(n) = n/P(n) (OPEN)
sections.summary: Documents the open characterization problem: which composite $n$ satisfy $f(n) = n/P(n)$? Known examples: all semiprimes $pq$ (by `f_semiprime`) and $n = 30$ (by `f_30`). The general characterization remains open; $f(n) = n/P(n)$ does NOT hold for all composite $n$.
sections.mathContext: Open question: characterize $\{n \text{ composite} : f(n) = n/P(n)\}$. Known: all semiprimes $pq$ satisfy this, as do some non-semiprimes like $30$. A false axiom claiming this holds for all composite $n$ was identified and removed.

sections.title: Question 2: Large Values of f(n)
sections.summary: PROVES `f_prime_square`: $f(p^2) \ge p = \sqrt{p^2}$ from `f_lower_bound` and `minFac_prime_sq`. Axiomatizes `erdos_700_question2`: infinitely many composite $n$ with $f(n) > \sqrt{n}$. Prime squares give equality ($f(p^2) \ge p = \sqrt{p^2}$), so strict inequality is the open part.
sections.mathContext: Proved: $f(p^2) \ge p$, since $p(p^2) = \text{minFac}(p^2) = p$ and $p(n) \le f(n)$. Open: are there infinitely many composite $n$ with $f(n) > \sqrt{n}$ strictly? Prime squares are sparse ($\sim \sqrt{x}/\log x$ up to $x$), and they only achieve $f(p^2) \ge \sqrt{n}$, not strict inequality.

sections.title: Question 3: Upper Bound Conjecture
sections.summary: Axiomatizes `erdos_700_question3`: for every $A > 0$, $\exists C > 0$ such that $f(n) \le C \cdot n / (\log n)^A$ for all composite $n \ge 4$. This would show $f(n)$ is much smaller than $n/P(n)$ for typical $n$, since $P(n) \sim \log n$ by Hardy-Ramanujan.
sections.mathContext: Open conjecture: $f(n) \ll_A n/(\log n)^A$ for every fixed $A > 0$. This would imply $f(n)/n \to 0$ faster than any power of $1/\log n$. The connection to the Hardy-Ramanujan theorem: $P(n) \sim \log n$ for typical $n$, so $n/P(n) \sim n/\log n$, and the conjecture asks whether $f(n)$ is typically much smaller than even this.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős and Szekeres studied the arithmetic of binomial coefficients throughout the mid-20th century, producing many results on divisibility patterns in Pascal's triangle. Problem 700 investigates $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \leq n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$, which measures the minimum common divisor between $n$ and its non-trivial binomial coefficients. The function is closely tied to Kummer's theorem (1852), which determines $v_p(\binom{n}{k})$ by counting carries in base-$p$ addition of $k$ and $n-k$. For semiprimes $n = pq$, one can show $f(pq) = p$ using the fact that $\binom{pq}{p}$ is divisible by $q$ but $\gcd(pq, \binom{pq}{p}) = p$. The identity $f(30) = 6$ shows the characterization extends beyond semiprimes. The three open questions probe the boundary between exact characterization, extreme behavior, and typical asymptotics, connecting to the distribution of prime factors and the anatomy of integers.
overview.problemStatement: For composite $n$, define $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \leq n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$. Three questions: (1) Which composite $n$ satisfy $f(n) = n/P(n)$? (2) Do infinitely many composite $n$ have $f(n) > \sqrt{n}$? (3) Is $f(n) \ll_A n/(\log n)^A$ for all $A > 0$?
overview.text: Study f(n) = min_{1<k≤n/2} gcd(n, C(n,k)). When does f(n) = n/P(n)? Are there ∞ many n with f(n) > √n? Is f(n) ≪ n/(log n)^A? Known: f(pq) = p, f(p²) ≥ p. Open.
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines $f(n)$ via `Finset.min'` over `Finset.Icc 2 (n/2)` (nonempty for $n \geq 4$), proving the range is nonempty. Two theorems are proved: `minFac_prime_sq` ($\text{minFac}(p^2) = p$ via `dvd_of_dvd_pow`) and `f_prime_square` ($f(p^2) \geq p$ from `f_lower_bound`). The sandwich bounds, semiprime values, and open questions remain axiomatized. A false axiom (claiming $f(n) = n/P(n)$ for all composite $n$) was identified and removed.
keyInsights: $f(pq) = p = n/P(n)$ for semiprimes provides the simplest exact computation, following from Kummer's theorem since the base-$p$ and base-$q$ carries in $\binom{pq}{k}$ are controlled by the single-digit structure

$f(p^2) \geq p = \sqrt{n}$ shows Question 2 has a positive answer for prime squares, but these are sparse ($\sim \sqrt{x}/\log x$ up to $x$), so the question is really about non-prime-square composites

The upper bound conjecture $f(n) \ll n/(\log n)^A$ would imply $f(n)/n \to 0$ faster than any power of $1/\log n$, suggesting $f$ is typically much smaller than the trivial bound $n/P(n)$ since $P(n) \sim \log n$ for typical $n$
The function $f$ detects the arithmetic structure of $n$ through the lens of Pascal's triangle: rows of Pascal's triangle modulo $n$ encode the base-$p$ digit structure for each prime $p \mid n$
$n = 30 = 2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$ with $f(30) = 6 = 30/5$ shows the characterization problem for Question 1 is nontrivial, since $30$ is not a semiprime yet still achieves the upper bound
prerequisites: **GCD and divisibility in the integers**: Properties of $\gcd(a,b)$ including $\gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$ for various $k$, and the relationship between common divisors and prime factorizations. Nat.gcd in Mathlib.

**Binomial coefficients and Pascal's triangle**: The definition $\binom{n}{k} = n!/(k!(n-k)!)$, the row structure of Pascal's triangle, and divisibility properties such as $p \mid \binom{p}{k}$ for prime $p$ and $0 < k < p$.

**Kummer's theorem on $p$-adic valuations**: Kummer's theorem (1852) that $v_p(\binom{m+n}{m})$ equals the number of carries when adding $m$ and $n$ in base $p$, which is the key tool for computing $\gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$ prime by prime.

**Largest and smallest prime factors**: The functions $P(n) = \max\{p : p \mid n\}$ and $p(n) = \min\{p : p \mid n\}$ (Nat.minFac), and the sandwich inequality $p(n) \le f(n) \le n/P(n)$ that bounds the GCD function.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem 700 poses three interrelated questions about $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \leq n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$. The formalization captures the sandwich bounds, exact values for semiprimes and $n=30$, the prime square lower bound, and all three open questions. The function connects the divisibility structure of binomial coefficients to prime factorization, with all questions remaining open.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: Resolution would deepen understanding of how prime factorizations interact with binomial coefficient divisibility.

Question 3 connects to the Hardy-Ramanujan theorem on the typical number of prime factors ($\omega(n) \sim \log \log n$) and to Kummer's theorem on $p$-adic valuations of binomial coefficients. A characterization for Question 1 would reveal structural conditions on $n$ ensuring maximal divisibility, potentially involving the digit structure of $n$ in all prime bases.
openQuestions: Which composite $n$ beyond semiprimes and $n = 30$ satisfy $f(n) = n/P(n)$? Is there a characterization in terms of the prime factorization of $n$?
Are there composite $n$ that are not prime squares with $f(n) > \sqrt{n}$? What is the density of such $n$?
Is $f(n) \ll_A n/(\log n)^A$ for every fixed $A > 0$? Can this be approached via estimates for $v_p(\binom{n}{k})$ using Kummer's theorem?
What is the average order of $f(n)$ over composite $n \leq x$? Does it connect to the Erdős-Kac theorem on $\omega(n)$?

crossReferences.description: Kummer's theorem on p-adic valuations of binomial coefficients is the key tool for computing f(n)
Wolstenholme's theorem gives special divisibility of binomial coefficients C(p,k) for primes p, a related but distinct phenomenon
